findings.title: Mutual exclusion check between `age` and `timestamp` ignores `0`
findings.body: `BrowserReportSerializer.validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` check `if self.initial_data.get("age"):` and `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp"):` using truthiness rather than `is not None`. Because `0` is a valid non-negative integer for both `age` (a report generated 0ms ago) and `timestamp` (`min_value=0`), a payload containing both fields where one of them is `0` (e.g. `{"age": 0, "timestamp": 1640995200000}`) will bypass the mutual-exclusion validation instead of raising a `ValidationError`. Also, a report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` is accepted even though both specs require one of the two.

findings.title: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` can pair event IDs with the wrong nodestore data
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` calls `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then iterates `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `get_multi` returns a dict keyed by `node_id` whose key order and completeness are not guaranteed to match `node_ids` (for example, some backends omit missing keys or return results in arbitrary order). Pairing `error_ids` positionally with `events.values()` can associate an `event_id` with another event's payload or silently drop events. Iterate over `zip(error_ids, node_ids)` and look up `events.get(node_id)` instead.

findings.title: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` are only filtered out when a search query is entered
findings.body: In `Attributes`, `sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns `sorted` directly when `!searchQuery.trim()` (lines 61-63), and only applies `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` inside the search filter branch (lines 65-69). As a result, `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` are still displayed in the attributes tree whenever the search bar is empty.
